decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual elbow-up right-arm approach above the workspace. Gray nut is on the right near the center; retain clearance while orienting downward.
Move right gripper inward above the gray nut while completing the downward orientation, keeping the left arm parked.
Center over the gray nut and descend slowly to the demonstrated nut-grasp height; leave the gripper open for visual alignment.
Fine-center the gray nut from the wrist view, close fully, then lift vertically to check retention.
Gray nut is visibly retained. Carry it above the matching gray bolt on the right, with vertical clearance before fine alignment.
Lower the retained gray nut toward its bolt with a small wrist-view lateral correction. Stop near engagement height for another alignment check.
Fine-align the gray nut over the shaft, lower to engagement, and begin a small clockwise tightening turn with the gripper closed.
The gray shaft is visible inside the nut. Continue a controlled clockwise turn with very slight axial descent, maintaining the grip.
Release the gray nut in place and rewind the open wrist for another tightening stroke; do not reverse the nut while gripping.
Regrasp and tighten the gray nut another clockwise stroke. In parallel, start the left arm's gradual elbow-up approach for the red nut without crossing workspaces.
Rewind the open right wrist without loosening the gray nut. Move the left gripper above the red nut and complete its downward orientation.
Continue gray-nut tightening with a closed-gripper clockwise stroke. Lower the open left gripper toward the red nut, stopping above final grasp depth for alignment.
Finish aligning and grasping the red nut with the left arm, then lift to check retention. Open and rewind the right wrist for the next gray tightening stroke.
Carry the visibly held red nut to the center staging area without crossing arms. Apply a fourth clockwise gray-nut tightening stroke with the right gripper closed.
Lower and release the red nut at the middle staging point for the right arm. Rewind the open right wrist for the final gray tightening stroke.
Withdraw the open left gripper from the staged red nut and clear the middle. Finish a fifth clockwise gray tightening stroke with the right arm.
Release the gray pair and lift the right gripper clear while restoring its pickup orientation. Park the left arm on its own side to allow a staged red-nut pickup.
Gray pair remains upright after release. Move the open right gripper above the red nut at the shared staging point while the left arm stays clear.
Descend the open right gripper toward the staged red nut. Keep the approach on the right side of the midpoint and inspect final alignment before closing.
Fine-center and grasp the staged red nut with the right arm, then lift vertically to check that it is retained before transferring to the red bolt.
The red nut is visibly retained. Lift for clearance and carry it above its matching red bolt on the right, keeping the other arm parked.
Lower the retained red nut over the matching red shaft, with a small wrist-view centering correction. Keep it upright and closed for engagement inspection.
Nudge the red nut toward the visible shaft center and begin a gentle clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial descent.
Complete the first red-nut clockwise stroke with slight axial descent, then release in place before rewinding.
Rewind the open right wrist while leaving the red nut on its shaft, preparing a second tightening stroke.
Regrasp and apply a second clockwise red-nut tightening stroke with a small axial descent; keep the other arm clear.
Release the red nut in place and rewind the open wrist for the third tightening stroke, without reversing the nut.
Apply the third controlled clockwise tightening stroke to the red nut, keeping it upright and the gripper closed.
Release and rewind the right wrist for a fourth red-nut tightening stroke, leaving the nut on the bolt.
Apply a fourth clockwise red-nut tightening stroke with the gripper closed and slight axial descent.
Open and rewind the right wrist for the fifth red-nut tightening stroke, leaving the upright pair undisturbed.
Finish the fifth clockwise red-nut stroke with a closed grip and minimal axial descent before releasing the pair.
Release the tightened red pair, lift clear, and restore the open right gripper's pickup orientation before approaching the remaining purple nut.
Move above the remaining purple nut on the right with clearance over the completed pairs, correcting the gripper to an upright pickup orientation.
Lower the open right gripper toward the purple nut, keeping the left arm clear and stopping for close-range alignment.
Fine-center the purple nut from the wrist view, lower to grasp height, close fully, and lift to verify retention before staging it for the left arm.
The purple nut is visibly retained. Lift for clearance and carry it to the center staging point for a sequential handover, keeping the left arm parked.
Lower the purple nut onto the center staging area and release it upright. The left arm remains parked until the right gripper has withdrawn.
Withdraw the open right gripper vertically from the staged purple nut, then move it back into its own workspace to clear the left-arm pickup.
Approach above the staged purple nut with the open left gripper while moving the right arm farther into its own workspace. Maintain a sequential handover and clearance.
Lower the open left gripper toward the staged purple nut, staying just left of the midpoint. Keep the right arm parked and inspect near-grasp alignment.
Fine-center and grasp the staged purple nut with the left arm, then lift vertically to verify retention before carrying it to the matching bolt.
The purple nut is visibly held. Lift for clearance and carry it over the matching purple bolt in the left workspace, with the right arm clear.
Lower the retained purple nut toward its matching shaft with a small lateral centering correction. Pause near engagement height to inspect alignment.
Correct the purple nut slightly toward the visible shaft center, then begin a gentle clockwise tightening stroke while maintaining an upright closed grip.
Make a small wrist-frame lateral correction to center the purple shaft, then complete the first clockwise stroke with minimal descent.
Release the purple nut in place and rewind the open left wrist for the next clockwise tightening stroke; inspect whether it stays seated on the shaft.
The purple nut remains seated after release. Apply its second clockwise tightening stroke while moving the open right arm to a clear return waypoint.
Release and rewind the left wrist for the next purple tightening stroke. Begin a gradual elbow-up right-arm return using small continuous increments.
Apply the third purple-nut tightening stroke while completing the right arm's slow return to its original open-gripper pose.
Release the purple nut in place and rewind the open left wrist for its fourth tightening stroke. Hold the right arm near its original pose.
Regrasp the seated purple nut and apply its fourth clockwise tightening stroke with slight axial descent, keeping the right gripper open at origin.
Release and rewind the left wrist for the fifth purple-nut tightening stroke. Keep the right arm open at its original pose.
Apply the fifth clockwise tightening stroke to the purple nut with minimal descent, keeping the right arm parked and open.
Release the purple pair, lift the open left gripper clear, and restore its approach orientation for a gradual return to origin.
All three pairs remain upright after release. Begin a slow, continuous left-arm return toward its original pose, with both grippers open.
Complete the left arm's gradual return to its original pose, leaving both grippers open and the three assembled pairs undisturbed.
Settle both open grippers at their original poses and check that the assembled pairs remain stationary after release.
The gray shaft still appears deeper in its nut than the other two. Reapproach slowly with the right arm for close inspection and, if needed, further tightening; leave the left arm at origin.
The clearer overhead view shows the gray shaft seated close to the nut rim. Avoid disturbing it; return the open right arm to origin and settle both arms.
The gray pair still exposes more internal threads than the other two in the close view. Reapproach gradually for additional tightening while leaving the red and purple pairs undisturbed.
Complete the upright right-gripper approach above the gray pair, retaining clearance before a final controlled tightening check.
Descend slowly to the gray nut's current height, square the gripper with its axis, and regrasp for one final tightening stroke without disturbing the other pairs.
Apply an additional controlled clockwise stroke to the gray nut, with slight axial descent and a closed grip. Keep the completed red and purple pairs undisturbed.
Release the gray nut and rewind the open wrist without reversing the nut. Its shaft still appears recessed, so prepare another controlled tightening stroke.
Allow the right gripper to close fully before applying another clockwise gray-nut tightening stroke with small axial descent.
Release the gray nut and rewind only the open wrist, preserving the assembled pair while preparing a final shallow tightening pass.
Regrasp the gray nut and make one final clockwise tightening pass with a shallow three-millimeter descent; then inspect before release and return.
Release the gray pair and lift the open right gripper clear while restoring its return orientation. Leave all three pairs undisturbed.
The gray pair remains upright after release. Begin a gradual right-arm return to origin, keeping both grippers open and the assembled pairs clear.
Complete the right arm's gradual return to its original pose with both grippers open, leaving all three assembled pairs untouched.
